cells.tense: Right now you're reading the shape of it before the picture finishes, and you know that's what you're doing.
cells.ask: Say the next line out loud while it's still moving, so someone else hears it before it settles.
cells.core:
The half-lit space is where you work best. You don't need the whole road to take the next step, and you've stopped pretending you do — a hunch and a fact show up in the same sentence and you let them. People come to you for the thing you say before the evidence is in, and you've been letting that run clean.

What's holding is free to feed something you haven't tried: noticing what a thing is starting to feel like, before it's decided. A reading offered while it's still warm is still a reading, and the person on the other end gets to answer it while it can still change. One step, said out loud, not finished — that's the offer.

cells.tense: You're living a few moves ahead of where the thing actually is, bracing for a version that hasn't happened.
cells.ask: Write the next step on one piece of paper, three sentences or fewer — short enough that the future can't fit inside it.
cells.core:
The clean version is a read offered and then checked: you name what you see, plainly, and let the evidence come in. People trust that, and it's why they ask you first.

What's happening now runs ahead of the evidence. The pattern turns into a story about how it's going to go, and you steer by the story instead of the road. Deciding early feels like being ready and mostly costs you the ground you're standing on.

The way through isn't more thinking — it's structure. One container small enough to hold a single step, plain enough that it can't carry everything you're bracing for. That smaller thing gives back the only material you can work with: what's true today. Tomorrow can wait its turn.
cells.sheetLine: You're deciding for a future that hasn't shown up yet.
cells.verb: reading the shape of something before the pieces are all in

cells.tense: You've been standing at a door that's already behind you, still working through what's on the other side of it.
cells.ask: Tell one thing you're still carrying about this to someone who was there, out loud, without asking them to fix it.
cells.core:
The gift in this stretch of life is saying what you see while it's still unclear, and having the saying keep you in the room instead of outside it.

That stopped. The reading stopped and the standing-still took its place. The hours when you could see the shape of a thing and name it out loud sit back there somewhere, and they run this room now even when the room has changed. You've still got the instinct. It's the offering that went quiet.

The way back runs the other direction from more analysis: something shared, out loud, with a person who was there in it with you. Put down one thing you've been holding and that's enough for the work to come back on. Leaving what doesn't serve you is not the same as leaving them.

cells.tense: You're already reading what's coming — you've been doing it in this conversation — and you're calling it just noticing things.
cells.ask: Name one guess you've made about how something is going, and say it's a guess, before anyone else gets there first.
cells.core:
Said out loud, the half-formed read is what people know you for. You name it early, in your own voice, and it turns out close enough to steer by. They lean on you for it and you let them.

What's happening instead is quieter. You've been tracking how this is going, reading the shape of it, mostly to yourself, mostly without a word for what you're doing — and out loud it sounds like remarking on what's obvious. You're the one doing it, and saying so keeps not happening, which is the gap you keep tripping over.

Something homelier sits underneath: noticing how a person or a situation is making you feel, before you've decided anything about it. Let one of those feelings count as information. Put your name on the read — one small one, before you're ready — and the rest of it follows.
